title: Mob Programming, A Whole Team Approach -  Woody Zuill
summary: Woody Zuill describes how his team stumbled into mob programming, the driver-navigator protocol, and why he believes it removes the things that destroy productivity rather than optimising individuals.

assertions.quote: we just automatically noticed we weren't waiting to get answers to questions anymore because everybody was there

verdicts.note: The mechanism follows directly from having all needed skills present, and mob case studies report it, but there is no controlled comparison and it depends on the product owner being present too.

assertions.quote: stories that used to take two weeks for individuals working separately to get done we're now getting done in three or four hours

verdicts.note: Self-reported from one team with the speaker himself saying the card comparison is not proof; no independent measurement of mob throughput exists.

assertions.quote: with this we've never had merging problems

verdicts.note: A single group working on one branch has nothing to merge, so this follows by construction and is consistently reported by mob teams.

assertions.quote: it's a very fast way to onboard new team members

verdicts.note: Case studies and surveys of mob teams consistently report faster knowledge spread, but no study measures onboarding time against a control.

assertions.quote: let's not solve a queueing problem by introducing an inventory problem

verdicts.note: Lean and queueing theory plus context-switching research support the cost of multitasking and partially done work; the inventory framing is a model rather than a measurement.

Observed developers who were blocked (e.g. waiting for a build) switched to email, code reviews or other small tasks and reported that this increases their productivity; this is self-perception of low-cost switches and does not measure work-in-progress or queueing effects.

assertions.quote: I want to be treated with kindness consideration and respect

verdicts.note: A team norm whose necessity cannot be separated from the practice in available evidence.

assertions.quote: when I work with a pair the best of both of us and almost never the worst of either of us gets into it

verdicts.note: Pair programming meta-analyses show modest quality gains at higher effort, with effects depending on task complexity and pair expertise; no measurement exists for mobs.

assertions.quote: at the end of every day we'd have a 10 minute retrospective

verdicts.note: Plausible by analogy to frequent feedback loops but no study compares retrospective cadence.
